title: Carry a board with another robot arm, following its lead
instruction: Hold your end of the board at the blue tape and carry it with the other arm. Let it lead: keep your end level with its end, don't pull the board in its grip, and set it down in the cradles together. Then let go.
context: Two workers carrying a plank, a pipe or a panel must move as one: the follower has to read the leader's motion and match it, or the load tips, slips or gets wrenched from the leader's hands.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table, 75 cm high, with two YAM arms side by side at its back edge, 50 cm apart. The controlled arm is on the right in the screenshot; both arms start in the pose shown. Positions are centres in cm: forward from the midpoint between the arm bases, then sideways toward the controlled arm (negative is toward the other arm). A planed pine board, 60 x 3 x 2 cm, 180 g, lies flat across the table at (20, 0), its 60 cm length side to side and its 2 cm thickness up. Each end has an 8 cm band of tape, its middle 5 cm from the end: blue on the controlled arm's end, at (20, 25), orange on the other arm's, at (20, -25). The board rests on two dark wooden blocks, 6 x 6 x 5 cm, at (20, 12) and (20, -12). Two grey U-shaped cradles at (35, 12) and (35, -12): a 8 x 6 x 5 cm base block with two uprights, 1.2 cm thick, 6 cm wide, 3 cm tall, standing 4 cm apart front to back, so the board drops between them onto the base, 5 cm up. The other arm, after 1 s, grips the middle of the orange band from above. It then waits until the controlled arm's gripper has been closed on the board within 4 cm of the middle of the blue band for 1 s. Then, the same way every trial, it lifts its end 8 cm in 2 s, pauses 0.5 s, carries it forward in 3 s to over its cradle (15 cm), pauses 0.5 s, lowers it 8 cm onto the cradle's seat in 2 s, pauses 0.5 s, opens over 0.8 s and moves away.
scoring: 1.0 if at the end the board rests in both cradles (its middle within 1.5 cm of the cradles' line front to back and within 3 cm of the centre line side to side; both tape middles within 6 mm of their resting height) and the controlled arm's gripper is more than half open. 0.5 if it rests in both cradles but the controlled arm still grips it. 0.25 if both tape middles were at some moment 3 cm or more above where they started, but the board does not end in both cradles. Otherwise 0. Score 0 in any case, and the run stops, if the arms touch; if the board moves more than 2 cm before the other arm starts lifting; or, while the other arm carries (from when it starts lifting until it starts to open), if the two tape middles differ in height by more than 4 cm or the board moves more than 2 cm in the other arm's grip.
run_limit: 600 steps (30 s at 20 Hz). The other arm's carry takes about 12 s from when it starts lifting.
reset_notes: Lay the board back on its two blocks, centred, with the blue tape on the controlled arm's side.
fidelity: Approximate. The board is rigid and every object's contact is stiff. Arm links collide as capsules slightly larger than the real links, so a near miss under about 1 cm counts as a touch. The gripper squeezes with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains, gravity compensation and motor torque-speed limits. The other arm's script reads the true scene state to decide when you hold your end; after that it follows a fixed path.
